lesson_title: Two Bowls: Income, Expenditure and the Household Budget
hook_text: Your payslip says R9 500. You will never touch R9 500. Here's where it actually goes.
clip_script: Put two bowls on the table. Everything that walks IN goes in the first bowl. Everything that walks OUT goes in the second. That's a budget — everything else is detail. Now the first surprise. The payslip says nine thousand five hundred at the top. You'll never see it. Three bites come out first: tax, seven-sixty. The unemployment fund, ninety-five — one rand for every hundred you earn. And four-seventy-five into a pension for the you of the future. That's one thousand three hundred and thirty gone, and eight thousand one hundred and seventy actually lands. THAT is the only number the in-bowl gets. Budgeting with the nine-five is like planning supper around a chicken your neighbour is holding. And now the mistake that ruins it: don't write "tax" in the out-bowl. It never came in, so it can't go out. Count it twice and your whole month is wrong. In-bowl minus out-bowl. Money left over is a surplus. Money short is a deficit — and a deficit always gets paid by somebody.
visual_style: A kitchen table, two enamel bowls, coins moving between them; a payslip with three bites visibly taken out of the top figure before the remainder drops into the first bowl.
mood: Warm and steady, like an aunt showing you the family finances for the first time.
pacing: Calm setup on the bowls, brisk through the three deductions, firm landing on surplus versus deficit.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and build a budget that survives a bad month.
